title: Support python 3.12 type Type = syntax
description:

## Description

`great-docs build` fails when using `type Type =` syntax from python 3.12. 
With
> API reference build failed: Cannot handle auto for object kind: Kind.TYPE_ALIAS 
## Reproducible example

Add the following to an existing documented package and run `great-docs build`

```
from typing import Literal
type Contract = Literal[“a”, “b”]

```

- [x] Post a minimal reproducible example (MRE) so the maintainer can troubleshoot the problems you identify. A reproducible example is:
  - [x] **Runnable**: post enough code and data so any onlooker can create the error on their own computer.
  - [x] **Minimal**: reduce runtime wherever possible and remove complicated details that are irrelevant to the issue at hand.
  - [x] **Readable**: format your code according to the [Style Guide for Python Code](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/).

## Expected result

Documentation build is successful or error message gives indication of how to resolve. I see no way to categorize objects by hand in the documentation.

## Development environment

- Operating System: [e.g., Linux, macOS, Windows]
- Great Docs Version: [e.g., 0.1.0]

## Additional context

maybe this is more of a feature request than a bug. 

I do have my own handwritten reference section, so I am a bit confused this runs. Also, `great-docs scan` runs with no errors.
